Fixed Space Heating, Cooling and Ventilation Equipment Manufacturing

merger_description:
Copeland IP Corporation (**Copeland**), a portfolio company controlled by funds advised and/or managed by affiliates of Blackstone Inc. (**Blackstone**) proposes to acquire MRC Dickson Holdings LLC (**MRC Dickson Holdings**) from MRC Dickson Equity LLC (the **Acquisition**).

MRC Dickson Holdings is a US-headquartered company with global operations, primarily active in North America. Through its Dickson brand, it provides fully integrated environmental monitoring solutions, predominantly for regulated life sciences applications.

Globally, Dickson designs, manufactures and commercialises hardware devices and software solutions for the monitoring of various environmental parameters (such as temperature, humidity, pressure and CO2 levels) in regulated environments.

MRC Dickson Holdings supplies to a small number of Australian customers directly and through distributors.

Copeland’s core business is heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) and refrigeration compression technologies for residential, commercial and industrial applications. It provides products and services for the climate control industry, including residential heating and cooling equipment, commercial air conditioning solutions, commercial and industrial refrigeration and monitoring solutions, and cold chain management solutions.

Blackstone is a US-based corporation, incorporated under the laws of Delaware, United States. Blackstone is an investment management firm.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
• there is no horizontal overlap between Copeland or
Blackstone’s controlled portfolio companies and MRC
Dickson Holdings in Australia
• there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of products or services post-
acquisition
• MRC Dickson Holdings has a small presence in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
